record.paper_title: Variational principles in grid generation and geometric modelling: theoretical justifications and open problems
record.original_question: For quasi-isometric parameterization of a manifold by cut-and-paste flattening, how should one choose an optimal finite set of cuts, for example cuts that reduce pocket depth and enable either global flattening with unfolding or flattening of polygons cut from the manifold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth compact two-dimensional manifold (possibly with boundary) embedded in $\mathbb{R}^3$, equipped with the induced Riemannian metric. A "cut system" on $M$ is a finite collection $\mathcal{C}$ of disjoint simple arcs and loops on $M$ such that the complement $M\setminus\mathcal{C}$, after a cut-and-paste operation, becomes a (possibly disconnected) surface that admits a parameterization $\varphi:M\setminus\mathcal{C}\to\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ into a planar domain $\Omega$. The parameterization $\varphi$ is called quasi-isometric with constant $K\ge 1$ if for every tangent vector $v$ one has
$$K^{-1}\|v\|\le\|d\varphi(v)\|\le K\|v\|.$$
For a point $p\in M$, define its "pocket depth" with respect to a cut system $\mathcal{C}$ as the intrinsic distance from $p$ to the nearest cut or boundary component, taken along paths that remain in the connected component of $M\setminus\mathcal{C}$ containing $p$.

Problem: Develop a constructive procedure that, given $M$ and a target distortion bound $K$, selects a finite cut system $\mathcal{C}$ which is optimal in the following sense:
(a) The complement $M\setminus\mathcal{C}$ admits a $K$-quasi-isometric flattening into the plane, either as a single global unfolding or as a union of planar polygons cut from $M$; and
(b) Among all cut systems satisfying (a), $\mathcal{C}$ minimizes a suitable functional measuring the total length (or number) of cuts and the maximum pocket depth.

Formulate precise existence, uniqueness, and characterization theorems for such optimal cut systems, and describe an algorithm to compute them.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of optimally choosing cuts for low-distortion (quasi-isometric) surface flattening remains an active research area. Heuristic methods such as OptCuts (jointly optimizing cuts and parameterization) and target-shape cutting frameworks have been developed, but no general theory characterizing optimal cut systems with provable pocket-depth and quasi-isometric distortion guarantees has been established. The problem appears open in its full generality.

status_evidence.title: OptCuts: joint optimization of surface cuts and parameterization
status_evidence.snippet: Joint optimization framework for surface cuts and UV parameterization to reduce distortion.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art methods address cut selection for parameterization heuristically rather than providing a complete theoretical characterization.

status_evidence.title: Surface Cutting and Flattening to Target Shapes
status_evidence.snippet: Novel framework for surface cutting and flattening, aligning boundaries with target shapes.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2024) work continues to develop new cutting/flattening frameworks, indicating the problem is not definitively resolved.

status_evidence.title: Near-isometric flattening of brain surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Quasi-isometric flattening methods for cortical surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Applications drive continued investigation of near-isometric flattening, with cut selection remaining a practical and theoretical challenge.
